What I built
A focus dashboard using Apple Watch heart-rate data and keyboard activity.
My contribution
Backend services and frontend–backend integration.
Result
A hackathon prototype with live data, focus scores, and audio alerts.

Contributor · Team of three · Hack The Hill III · September 2026

Hackathon scope

We prioritized connecting wearable data, backend services, and the dashboard over UI polish to meet the hackathon deadline.

Python, FastAPI, and WebSockets connect keyboard activity with Apple Watch heart-rate data ingested through Pulsoid.
Docker connects the services, with TimescaleDB storing the incoming time-series data.
The frontend presents the live signals and focus state, with ElevenLabs audio alerts supporting the notification flow.

What I built
A compact UNIX command interpreter in C with built-ins, pipelines, redirection, and background execution.
My contribution
A self-directed implementation to practice command parsing, POSIX processes, pipes, and file descriptors.
Result
Completed a working shell with nine built-in commands and external command execution.

Personal C programming exercise

Implemented nine built-in commands, including cd, pwd, echo, env, export, and history.
Used fork, execvp, and waitpid for external commands, with pipe and dup2 connecting command pipelines.
Added argument parsing, basic I/O redirection, background execution, and cleanup of command allocations.

heading: Poltergeist
text:
03 / SIMULATION LAB

Poltergeist
Ongoing
Read full case study ↗
View Poltergeist source
↗
What I built
A CARLA scenario runner and dashboard for evaluating autonomous driving agents.
My contribution
Scenario setup, simulator measurements, and the dashboard for reviewing recorded runs.
Result
Local runs with matched seeds, camera/LiDAR recordings, and behavior reports. Development is ongoing.

Autonomous driving simulation & evaluation

Intended users

I’m building this to pitch a repeatable stress-testing platform to autonomous-driving companies and startups.

Simulation measurements

I use CARLA position, speed, and timing data to calculate braking, stopping distance, clearance, and time to collision. The dashboard keeps units and unavailable measurements explicit.

Built a React and TypeScript dashboard with a FastAPI backend to create, save, validate, and execute parameterized driving scenarios.
Implemented repeatable agent comparisons with matched seeds, failure search, reproduction, and scenario minimization.
Linked agent observations and proposed/applied controls to telemetry, synchronized RGB camera and LiDAR recordings, and behavior reports.
Integrated a Python agent SDK and pretrained PlanT 2.0 reference controller for local driving experiments.
